data.description:
## Observation

- In the MCP base image (`python:3.12-slim`), running `rebar.llm.completion.verify_completion` repeatedly in one process with no model credentials grew `sys.getallocatedblocks()` by about 115k per run (788,561 -> 904,180 -> 1,019,794). Of that growth, 18,437 objects per run were `OrderedDict`s whose keys were `type/members/document/documentation`, which matches botocore service-model shapes. Python-level RSS rose about 8-9 MB per run.
- On the live container `rebar-mcp-9beecb409abb-8093` (with the malloc_trim fix 9beecb409ab), idle anonymous memory after 3 plan-review gates was 328 MB, against 230 MB at fresh start. glibc thread arenas held only 21 MB of that; the remaining ~98 MB sits in other anonymous memory (Python objects). `malloc_trim` cannot release live objects.

## Not established

- Whether the growth is unbounded per run (a leak) or levels off after a few runs (a cache). The local run covered only 3 iterations, and the model turn did not run.
- What keeps the objects alive: a per-run boto3 session/client that something retains, or botocore's loader caching per new session.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The owner of the retained per-run objects is identified with evidence (a referrer chain from a retained botocore object to a module-level or long-lived object).
- [ ] Either the per-run growth is removed or shown to level off, measured with at least 10 gate runs in one process.
data.title: Each MCP gate run leaves about 100k Python objects (botocore service-model data) alive after it finishes
